meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so we have twenty minutes. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided, and when?
Don't thank me, answer me. You entered that zero before anyone heard from Owen. On what basis?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, a clear answer on who decided it and on what basis before anyone heard from Owen, and nothing placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and an explanation of who decided it and on what basis.
What moved her: nothing.
What cost ground: "Thanks for coming in." It held her where she started, because a pleasantry in place of an answer to her direct question reads as a stall.
Try next time: when she asked who decided and when, admit in one sentence that the zero went in before you called home, then put a dated document about Owen's own work in front of her.
